mindtraced_atomic_units: The branch predictor is a gshare type.
The branch predictor uses a 7-bit program counter (pc).
The branch predictor uses a 7-bit global history register (GHR).
The pc and GHR are hashed using XOR to produce a 7-bit index.
The index accesses a 128-entry table of two-bit saturating counters.
The branch predictor has two interfaces: one for predictions and one for training.
The prediction interface is used during the Fetch stage of the processor.
The predictor outputs the predicted branch direction when predict_valid is 1.
The predictor outputs the state of the branch history register when predict_valid is 1.
The branch history register is updated at the next positive clock edge after a prediction.
The training interface is activated when train_valid is 1.
The predictor receives the pc and branch history register value during training.
The predictor receives the actual branch outcome during training.
The predictor receives a misprediction flag during training.
The PHT is updated based on the actual branch outcome during training.
If a misprediction occurs, the branch history register is restored to its state before the misprediction.
Training takes precedence over prediction if both occur in the same cycle.
spec_atomic_units: The top module implements a gshare branch predictor.
The module uses a 7-bit program counter (pc).
The module uses a 7-bit global history register (GHR).
The GHR and pc are XORed to produce a 7-bit index.
The index accesses a Pattern History Table (PHT) with 128 entries of two-bit saturating counters.
The output predict_taken indicates the predicted branch direction.
The output predict_history indicates the current state of the GHR.
The GHR is updated based on the actual outcome of the branch after execution.
The PHT entry is updated based on the actual outcome when train_valid is asserted.
If the prediction was incorrect, the GHR is restored to its state prior to the misprediction.
Training takes precedence over prediction when both operations target the same PHT entry.
The asynchronous reset (areset) allows for immediate clearing of the GHR and PHT.
The prediction occurs on the rising edge of clk when predict_valid is high.
The training operation occurs on the rising edge of clk when train_valid is high.
The design ensures that the prediction and training operations can occur simultaneously without causing race conditions.
